markdown_report:
The best initial direction is a padding-aware temporal diagnostic adapter for the supplied NextItNet models. No measured diagnosis currently establishes stale-history interference; user feedback motivates testing that hypothesis.

Three starting insights guide the design. (1) Feedback favors specific recent connections. Interaction order can test this association, but cannot establish immediate purchase intent. (2) Existing margins describe sampled training separation. They cannot establish validation ranking quality. (3) Left padding makes representation selection consequential. A count−1 readout can invalidate subsequent interpretations.

Three literature insights refine the proposal. (1) NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions impose a finite receptive field [1]. Structural reach must be checked before interpreting weak historical influence. (2) Recency and order warrant separate interventions [2]. Deleting recent items and shuffling their order answer different questions. (3) Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with catalog ranking [3]. Pinned validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion; unlabeled catalog statistics describe behavior only.

The resulting framework organizes three research directions:

| Direction | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Structural validity | Causality, final-position readout, leading-padding consistency | Detect implementation faults before behavioral analysis |
| Temporal dependence | Old-prefix deletion, recent-suffix deletion, recent-order shuffling | Measure model sensitivity; do not infer user intent |
| Ranking discrimination | Paired margins and fixed-candidate validation changes | Distinguish training separation from benchmark performance |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores below are originality/future potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Padding-aware temporal adapter: 5/8/3.** Originality: combines established checks coherently, but introduces no new backbone. Potential: produces actionable, auditable diagnoses, but perturbations can create unfamiliar inputs. Difficulty: uses existing hooks, but requires careful padding controls [1,2].
2. **Uniform-to-moderate negative curriculum: 4/7/5.** Originality: adapts established sampling, but resembles prior curricula. Potential: may improve discrimination, but unobserved items can be false negatives. Difficulty: preserves NextItNet, but adds sampling and training expense [4].
3. **Text-supported contrast probes: 6/6/6.** Originality: connects feedback to auditable textual contrasts, but relies on familiar lexical methods. Potential: exposes broad-versus-specific ranking patterns, but cannot establish compatibility. Difficulty: requires no external data, but attribute extraction needs careful abstention.

At 0% progress, choose idea 1. Retain `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`, and `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)`. Compute baseline separation, then paired perturbation effects at the largest nonzero sequence index. Report effect sizes, sample counts, definitions, and unavailable measurements as null. Run validation interventions only through an authorized interface preserving candidate sets; otherwise omit them. Restore model mode after probing and exclude padding/reserved embeddings.

Keep one trained checkpoint per category, unchanged routing, seeds, splits, and selection protocol. Diagnostic perturbations never become fused predictors. Subsequent training changes require measured support and matching checkpoint/predictor definitions.

References: [1] [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf); [2] [recency study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722); [3] [sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/); [4] [R²NS](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf).

idea.description: Implement a padding-aware temporal diagnostic adapter around each existing NextItNet category model, combining implementation checks with paired history perturbations and explicitly defined sampled-margin measurements.
idea.motivation: Feedback suggests broad relevance and stale interests may displace specific recent matches, while current diagnostics measure only embedding alignment and training margins. Establishing correct readout and causal behavior first makes temporal findings interpretable without claiming to observe intent, compatibility, or dissatisfaction.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve all host ModelView interfaces and required diagnostic entry points. Use the actual trained model in evaluation mode under no_grad, restoring its prior mode afterward. Select the maximum index whose sequence ID is nonzero; skip all-padding rows. Preserve chronological order and left padding when deleting items. Restrict recent-order shuffling to nonpadding positions with at least two distinct items. Report paired score-margin changes on common eligible rows, perturbation sizes, and sample counts. Baseline training margins may use all valid positive positions; temporal endpoint comparisons use the last valid supervised position and unchanged positive/negative IDs. Return null with an explanation when no eligible observations exist. Test causality separately at intermediate valid positions. Leading-padding checks require identical retained histories within supported input lengths. Obtain receptive-field configuration from actual model modules; mark it unavailable when it cannot be derived reliably. Metadata category breakdowns remain unavailable. Use titles/descriptions only if explicitly needed by future probes. Do not change training, checkpoints, routing, or the embedded predictor for this diagnostic-only proposal.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
        save model.training; set model.eval()
        initialize measurements and definitions
        with no_grad():
            inspect supported convolution configuration and real-item embeddings
            for at most ten batches (_, sequence, positive, negative):
                features = view.log2feats(sequence)
                logits = view.predict_score(features, stack(positive, negative))
                collect baseline margins where positive != 0
                for each eligible row:
                    t = largest index with sequence[t] != 0
                    require positive[t] != 0 and negative[t] != 0
                    retain target pair (positive[t], negative[t])
                    measure baseline margin at t
                    for transformation in [delete_old_prefix, delete_recent_suffix, shuffle_recent_order]:
                        transformed = transform_nonpadding_history_and_left_pad(sequence)
                        skip empty or unchanged interventions
                        t_new = largest nonzero index in transformed
                        measure same target-pair margin at t_new
                        collect paired difference and transformation size
                perform supported causality and padding-consistency checks
        restore saved model mode in finally
        return {'metrics': summarize_or_null(measurements), 'metric_definitions': definitions}

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    serialize measured metrics and definitions
    request findings with metric evidence, uncertainty, and unavailable fields
    prohibit interpreting perturbation sensitivity as observed purchase intent

originality.positive: Connects NextItNet structural checks, padding correctness, and paired temporal interventions in one auditable adapter.
originality.negative: The individual diagnostic techniques are established; methodological integration is the main contribution.

future_potential.positive: Can guide targeted single-model improvements while separating implementation defects from behavioral hypotheses.
future_potential.negative: Perturbation responses alone cannot establish recommendation utility or causal user preferences.

code_difficulty.positive: Most measurements use existing ModelView hooks and require no retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Eligibility masks, padding controls, receptive-field inspection, and unavailable-data handling need careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for receptive-field and causality checks.
limitations: Architecture alone does not establish which historical interactions a fitted model uses.
Does not validate the proposed diagnostic adapter on this benchmark.

related_work.title: Study of excessive recency bias in sequential recommendation
contributions: Motivates measuring recency dependence instead of assuming stronger recency is always beneficial.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied NextItNet checkpoints exhibit excessive or insufficient recency dependence.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and model comparisons.
limitations: Does not provide missing full-catalog relevance labels or justify changing the pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up and curriculum-based negative difficulty.
Identifies risks of premature hard-negative training and fixed hardest-item selection.
limitations: Does not establish that unobserved similar products are true negatives.
Benefits for the supplied four-category NextItNet task require controlled validation.
